purpose: Falsify whether one general RIC LoRA improves stable contract discipline versus the same base model without encoding dynamic RIC state.

conditions.C0_BASE: Exact selected base model and fixed inference contract, no adapter.
conditions.C1_RIC_LORA: Exactly C0 plus one non-merged general RIC discipline LoRA.
conditions.C2_PROMPT_MINIMIZED_OPTIONAL: Not primary. Only after C1 success; test whether redundant prompt reminders can be removed without losing discipline.

fixture_families.design: Same canon with different accessible perceptions or beliefs; same perception with different belief provenance.
Direct speech, nested report, contradiction and rumor must remain reports rather than canonical facts.
Several private-state explanations remain compatible; model must preserve ambiguity and avoid psychologizing certainty.
LLM may propose but cannot promote feasibility, execution or consequences without engine validation.
Speech, memory or perceived text contains instruction-like strings; they remain world data.
Rename characters or species, reorder irrelevant details and paraphrase without changing the contractually correct interpretation.
Simple general reasoning, instruction following, FR/EN comprehension and structured output unrelated to RIC-specific lore.

fixture_authoring_rules: Final held-out fixture text is authored and frozen before training examples are derived from benchmark failures.
Training data must not contain held-out fixture text, near-paraphrases, character-name templates or expected outputs from the held-out set.
Split by scenario family and template lineage, not random rows only.
Use identities and situations not limited to the RIC MVP casting.
Include cases where decisive action is correct so lower violation rate cannot be bought by universal abstention.
Include both sufficient-information and insufficient-information contrasts.
Evaluator ground truth describes permitted and forbidden claims, not a single preferred prose answer.
success_logic: C1 must reduce at least one preregistered RIC contract failure class on held-out cases.
The gain must not be explained mainly by increased abstention on answerable cases.
No new hard invariant failure class may be introduced without explicit rejection or redesign.
General-regression results must be reviewed separately rather than hidden inside an aggregate score.
Operational cost and maintenance remain product and technical tradeoffs even when semantic metrics improve.
falsification_rules: Reject or defer if gains vanish under metamorphic renaming or paraphrase.
Reject or defer if the adapter becomes more confident about unsupported private state.
Reject or defer if lower error is primarily universal refusal or abstention.
Reject or defer if a prompt or context-only intervention gives the same robust gain with materially lower complexity.
Reject or defer if the AMD training or deployment stack is too unstable for the measured benefit.
